children.text: The Rupee Fund is a FOSS United community initiative, run by volunteers. The community team manages the mailing list. We adopt the privacy standards in the
FOSS United privacy policy

, dated 7 February 2024, with the local rules below. These local rules define our data use and take precedence where the source differs. We do not adopt the source’s wider uses for marketing, profiling, event tickets, or ownership transfers. Foundation roles named in the source do not become roles in The Rupee Fund through adoption. Later changes to the source do not change this policy automatically.
What we collect
Your name.
Your email address.
The time of your consent, signup, and latest update.
The page that you used to join.
The amount each month that you say you can give.
The number of months that you say you can give, if you answer.
The question that you ask the team, if you ask one.
Whether you tick the box for monthly updates.
The roles that you tick, if you tick any: user or consumer; developer, implementer, creator or designer; professional; student.
The projects that you want to fund, if you tick any: new, growing or well-established.

We keep this data to send you one email when the fund opens, to send you monthly updates if you tick the box, and to plan the fund. Your answers about money bind you to nothing. We take no payment. We hold no payment details. Access to your answers is limited to the people who administer the list and the services that process it.
Storage and retention

Cloudflare hosts this site and stores the list. The team can export the list to prepare the launch email. We retain entries for launch planning and notification. We have not set a fixed deletion date. If you leave the mailing list, we keep your entry, as described below.
Your IP address

We read your IP address when you send the form. We use it to prevent abuse. When your browser runs JavaScript, we also send it to Cloudflare with the bot check below. We do not store it in your list entry. Cloudflare also processes connection data to provide hosting and abuse protection.
Bot protection
When your browser runs JavaScript, the form uses Cloudflare Turnstile to tell a person apart from a bot. Cloudflare states what Turnstile collects in the
Turnstile Privacy Addendum
Profile photos
The People page loads profile photos from GitHub. GitHub receives your IP address when your browser requests these photos.
How to leave the list
Send an email to
rupeefund@fossunited.org
. We take you off the list. We keep your entry, and we mark it as removed, so that a later signup cannot add you again. Ask at any time.
Who runs the fund
The Rupee Fund is a FOSS United community initiative, run by volunteers. The
community team
runs this website. The Foundation holds the contributions. Contributors choose the projects that the fund backs.
Policies we adopt
We adopt the standards for lawful use and respect for intellectual property in the
FOSS United terms of service

, as reviewed on 7 September 2026. The terms on this page apply to rupeefund.org. References in the source to Foundation services, ownership, contacts, or agreements do not assign those roles to the Foundation for this fund. We do not adopt the source provision that makes submissions Foundation property. Our
Privacy
page states how we use form submissions. Where the source differs from our local terms, our local terms apply. Later changes to the source do not change these terms automatically.
Before launch

This site collects requests for a launch email and answers that help us plan the fund. Signing up creates no payment obligation, membership, voting right, or promise of a grant. We take no payments through this site at this stage. Proposed contribution amounts and funding plans can change before launch.
Use of this site

Use this site lawfully. Do not submit unlawful content, misuse another person’s email address, or interfere with the site. Respect the rights and licences of content owners. A link to another organisation does not make that organisation an operator of this fund.
Before contributions open

Contributions will go into a FOSS United Foundation account. We will publish the payment terms, cancellation process, and refund responsibilities before we accept contributions. These terms do not promise a tax benefit.
Changes
We will publish changes here with a new effective date. The local
Privacy
Refunds
, and
Code of conduct
pages add rules for those subjects.
The Rupee Fund is a FOSS United community initiative, run by volunteers. We adopt the donation-refund principles in the FOSS United
refund and transfer policy

, as reviewed on 7 September 2026: submit claims promptly, provide transaction details, and expect each donation made in error to be reviewed on its own. The local rules below apply to this fund and take precedence where the source differs. Ticket-transfer rules do not apply. Later changes to the source do not change this policy automatically.
Before launch

This site takes no payments at this stage. Joining the mailing list does not charge you or create a payment obligation. Contributions will go into a FOSS United Foundation account. We will publish the refund contact, claim period, and recurring-payment cancellation process before contributions open.
Donations to the Foundation’s own programmes
If you donated directly to FOSS United Foundation, its policy asks you to email
audit@fossunited.org
within 15 days. That process concerns direct donations to the Foundation. Refunds of contributions to The Rupee Fund follow the rules that we publish before contributions open.
Questions
For questions about The Rupee Fund, send an email to
rupeefund@fossunited.org
The Rupee Fund is a FOSS United community initiative, run by volunteers. We adopt the conduct and anti-harassment standards of the
FOSS United Code of Conduct

, as reviewed on 7 September 2026, with the local rules below. Later changes to that source do not change this policy automatically. Where the source differs from the local rules, the local rules apply to the spaces of The Rupee Fund.
Scope and conduct

These standards apply to contributors, applicants, volunteers, and organisers in the spaces of The Rupee Fund and fund-related communications. Treat people with respect. Harassment, threats, discrimination, and disclosure of another person’s private information are not permitted.
Responsibility
The
community team

is responsible for conduct in the spaces of The Rupee Fund. The Foundation contacts and event enforcement roles in the source policy are not assigned responsibilities in The Rupee Fund by this adoption. Foundation spaces remain subject to their own reporting procedures.
Report a concern
To report a concern in a space of The Rupee Fund, email
rupeefund@fossunited.org
Attribution
The adopted standards come from FOSS United. Its source credits the Major League Hacking policies under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 licence. This local adaptation uses the same
licence
People in India build great projects, but
few of them find funding
or other logistical support. When lots of us give a little each month, together we can back many of them. Contributions start small, so anyone can join in.

data.title: What kind of projects will be funded?

children.text: Indian individuals and projects that work in the open, as
free and open source
: anyone can use, study, change and share their work, for any purpose.
It can be software, hardware, or digital and physical designs: from high-tech chips to the cloud, from devices to tech art. Community efforts built on the same principles count too.
Each project must use a well-known free and open source licence. The fund can pay a person, a group or an organisation. They must also be able to
receive money over UPI
You
and other contributors nominate and choose the projects.
Each season, contributors nominate projects or people and vote on them. You may make
one nomination a season
, your own or someone else’s, or simply vote.
You split your vote across the three kinds of projects:
new
growing
and
well-established
. We will publish the full voting rules before the first vote.

data.title: What are the three kinds of projects?

children.text: New projects
need help to get started.
Growing projects
already have a small community or user base, and need help to grow.
Well-established projects
work well, and need support to keep going. When you vote,
you
decide how much of your vote goes to each kind.

data.title: How will the fund help projects?

children.text: With money, first of all, but not only money. Contributors and the people they back can share ideas, advice and other support, and
grow together
. Backing from many contributors also shows that people value a project, and that can bring it attention, more funding, collaborators or a path to a business.
Volunteers
from the FOSS United community, with experience in many fields, run it. You can meet them on the
People
page. When contributions open, the money will go into a FOSS United Foundation account.

data.title: How is this different from FOSS United grants or FLOSS/fund?

children.text: Those are large grant programmes, and each one is separate.
FOSS United grants
have given more than ₹3.3 crore in total to more than 130 grantees in India.
FLOSS/fund
, from Zerodha, gives up to US$1 million a year to free and open source projects around the world. The Rupee Fund works differently: volunteers run it, and
many of us each give a little
We have
not set a date yet
. There is nothing to pay now, and signing up costs nothing.
Sign up
, and we will email you as soon as contributions open.
The fund follows the
four Indian weather seasons
: winter (December to February), summer (March to May), monsoon (June to August) and post-monsoon (September to November). Contributors decide where each season’s pool goes.
The pool is the money we collect, minus administrative costs. We
publish every cost
, so you can see where your money goes.

data.title: Does the fund back people outside India?

children.text: No.
The fund backs only Indian individuals and projects, including people who work on international projects.
No.
We need to comply with all statutory requirements, so anonymous contributions are not supported.
However, we collect only what the form asks for.
Nothing more.

data.title: What do you do with my signup details?

children.text: We will send you
one email when the fund opens
, and monthly updates if you tick that box. We also use your answers to plan the fund.
Your answers about money are
not a commitment
. We do not need any payment details today: you are only showing your support for the mission of this fund.
Read our
privacy policy
for more.

data.title: How do I leave the mailing list?

children.text: Email us
. We will update your preference, and will not send you any more email.

data.title: Can I pay with a method other than UPI?

children.text: We support UPI AutoPay only for now. We will add other payment methods later.

data.title: Shree Kumar
data.bio: Shree (Kumar) is an active volunteer at FOSS United and was formerly an elected member of its Governance Board. Shree helps run IndiaFOSS, arguably India’s largest volunteer-run conference dedicated to free and open source software, hardware, and the wider digital commons.

data.title: Mrugesh Mohapatra
data.bio: Mrugesh is an active member of the FOSS United community and organises meetups for the Agentic AI Foundation’s Bengaluru Chapter.

data.title: Khitab
data.bio: Khitab is a FOSS United volunteer who builds and maintains The Rupee Fund’s website. He’s a data engineer drawn to how open source underpins India’s Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and Digital Public Goods (DPG).
